transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-18
Start time: 15:30 PDT
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Maya Lin (Redwood AE), Samir Kapoor (Redwood SE), Lena Park (Cascade VP Eng), Diego Ruiz (Cascade SRE), Amir Patel (Cascade CTO)

Summary:
Short follow-up from the incident on 2027-03-15 where Cascade saw a spike in tail latency and a partial failover to degraded model variants under load. Goal: confirm facts, review mitigations, agree next steps for runbooks, tuning and Dedicated/reservation options.

Topics:
- Incident timeline and suspected root cause (autoscaling race + KV cache eviction patterns)
- Short-term mitigations (rate limiting, scaling policy changes, model variant fallback)
- Long-term reliability improvements (Dedicated capacity, canary rollouts, observability additions)
- Security/compliance asks (audit logs, KMS integration)

Action items (captured briefly above)

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: alright hi everyone thanks for hopping on, we'll do a quick recap and then Samir will walk through the runtime traces we pulled, um if that's okay?
[00:12] Lena: yep thanks, want to make sure we cover timeline cause procurement is also asking for a clear mitigation plan.
[00:20] Samir: cool, so quick context, our initial root cause is a concurrent autoscale + KV cache eviction scenario. when the burst hit the dispatcher we saw node churn, some KV cache entries dropped and that forced cold starts on some sequences leading to tail latencies up to 1.8s for 512-token requests.
[00:38] Diego: 1.8s was observed in production; our SLAs for that route are 300ms p95, so yeah that was bad. we also saw request retries hitting the routing policy which bumped load on fallback clusters.
[00:57] Amir: can you explain the routing bump? we thought fallback is only for region outage not load.
[01:05] Samir: right so Redwood's smart routing will try to fallback to cheaper / lower-tier variant if primary capacity is constrained — in this case the policy was set to allow variant fallback, and when nodes started to drop requests the fallback cluster accepted some traffic which then had lower batch efficiency, so cost went up and latency stayed high for some requests. there's also a configuration nuance where the autoscaler cooldowns were too short and we raced scale-up with cache warmup.
[01:35] Lena: is this a product bug or misconfig? we need to tell execs.
[01:39] Samir: leaning config + tuning. runtime behaved as designed but default autoscale/cooldown wasn't ideal for Cascade's P95 token lengths. we did observe a small regression when the model quantization path hit a kernel not yet optimized on that hardware — that added 70ms per token for a subset of sequences. transcription note: we might have mis-identified the kernel name in the trace.
[02:10] Diego: ok, what are the immediate mitigations? we already rolled a temporary rate limit to reduce concurrency but need something more durable.
[02:18] Maya: short-term we propose three things: 1) tighten routing policy to disable variant fallback for this critical route; 2) increase autoscaler target and cooldowns to avoid scale races; 3) enable prefix KV cache pinning for hot prompts so cache isn't evicted on scale events.
[02:40] Amir: prefix pinning — is that something we can configure or will Redwood need to change runtime?
[02:45] Samir: it's configurable. we can set certain prompts / templates to be sticky in cache, and Redwood will pre-warm on scale events if you provide the list. we'll share a script.
[02:57] Diego: we have a few top prompts, will share those.
[03:02] Samir: great. Medium-term: recommending a Dedicated pool for critical routes. Dedicated removes noisy neighbor effects, gives reserved GPU capacity and predictable throughput; also enables stricter isolation for your tokens and easier canary testing. downside is cost, but we can size a burst lane to keep costs reasonable.
[03:22] Lena: can you quantify cost delta for us — like baseline host vs dedicated plus burst?
[03:27] Maya: yep I'll send a pricing addendum; rough ballpark is 30-40% higher for a small Dedicated pool but unit token cost drops at sustained throughput, and you get better p95 guarantees. we'll include a scenario spreadsheet.
[03:41] Amir: on the security side, what about KMS and audit logs? procurement wants assurance around key access and SOC2 scope.
[03:49] Samir: Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and HSM, and we can push detailed audit logs into your SIEM. for hosted we have managed KMS and audit logs with retention tiers; we'll share SOC2 + ISO artifacts and a compliance checklist.
[04:09] Diego: we also need RBAC so only certain apps can call admin APIs.
[04:14] Samir: RBAC supported; we'll map roles to your IDP via SAML/SCIM integration.
[04:21] Lena: great. any blocker on us running a bench harness in staging? we want to reproduce the tail latency.
[04:27] Samir: none — we will hand over a benchmark harness and a guide to run it against staging. recommend using a mix of variable token lengths and spike patterns to simulate your traffic. include a warmup phase for KV cache.
[04:40] Diego: will do. by the way, we tried to run an in-house PoC last month but the self-hosted stack missed some perf kernels you're using.
[04:49] Maya: yeah folks often see that — our compilation layer picks kernels based on sequence distribution and hardware; some open-source stacks lag on the optimized nv and amd kernels.
[05:00] Amir: from a reliability standpoint we want a runbook: if p95 > 500ms alert, then switch routing to failfast and scale to Dedicated burst lanes, escalate to ops. can Redwood support automation around that?
[05:12] Samir: yes we can expose webhooks for alerts and auto-roll policies; we can also provide a canary rollout blueprint to validate new model versions or kernel builds.
[05:22] Lena: ok let's add that to the action items, and schedule a canary run.
[05:25] Maya: noted. quick question from procurement — what about data residency? some EU users must not leave region.
[05:31] Samir: Redwood can pin region routing and support private VPC deployments; for EU-bound data we can deploy model endpoints in EU region and enforce region routing. We'll include region residency options in the doc.
[05:45] Amir: any timeline for the kernel optimization you mentioned? the 70ms per token impact is material.
[05:52] Samir: engineering can triage, but we need a repro from your harness and the exact GPU/hardware specs; once we have that we're usually able to prioritize kernel selection or fallback to a precompiled variant within 1-2 sprints.
[06:07] Lena: ok we'll send details.
[06:10] [10:00 silence removed]
[06:18] Diego: small nit, our observability needs a per-token breakdown — not just p95 but token-by-token latency across KV hits/misses. do you expose that?
[06:26] Samir: we expose token-level tracing in the Redwood Console and can add a per-route breakdown; some traces are sampled due to overhead, but we can increase sampling for your critical route during the investigation window.
[06:40] Maya: I'll make sure we enable higher sampling for the next 48 hours once we sync logs.
[06:47] Lena: thanks. anything else on fixes?
[06:50] Samir: just one more — we saw a few client retries that amplified load. recommend adding jittered exponential backoff client-side and short-circuiting retries for known 5xx classes.
[07:03] Amir: yep we can push that change in client SDK.
[07:07] Lena: recap and next steps?
[07:09] Maya: recap: Samir to share trace + low-level timeline and suggested config changes by 2027-03-20; Diego to provide node logs by 2027-03-20; Maya to send pricing and Dedicated scenarios by 2027-03-19; Cascade to run benchmark harness and report by 2027-03-25; schedule follow-up the week of 2027-03-29 to review canary plan and runbook.
[07:32] Diego: sounds good. appreciate the fast turnaround on this.
[07:36] Amir: yes thanks, this was productive.
[07:38] Maya: thanks everyone. we'll follow up in email with the artifacts and links: incident timeline doc, runtime traces, benchmark harness repo, and pricing spreadsheet.
[07:48] Lena: thanks all, bye.

End of transcript.
